speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Given your symptoms of fatigue, weight loss, night sweats, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes, I need to ask a few specific questions to narrow this down. Have you experienced any recent fevers, or have you noticed any changes in your skin or bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your significant weight loss and night sweats, have you noticed any pain in your right upper abdomen or any itching on your skin recently? Also, have you experienced any difficulty swallowing or pain when drinking liquids?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, LFTs, ESR, CRP, LDH, and HIV status. REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound of supraclavicular nodes and abdominal ultrasound. Have you had any recent travel or exposure to tuberculosis?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC with differential shows Elevated WBC, Slightly Decreased Hemoglobin, and Normal Platelets; LFTs are not listed in the provided data; ESR is not listed in the provided data; CRP is not listed in the provided data; LDH is Elevated; HIV status is not listed in the provided data. Ultrasound of supraclavicular nodes shows massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes per CT correlation; Abdominal ultrasound shows Splenomegaly and dullness over the left lower quadrant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), painless supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, elevated LDH, splenomegaly, and the specific ultrasound findings of massive mediastinal and cervical lymph node involvement is highly characteristic. Given the significant weight loss and fixed nature of the nodes, I recommend initiating a biopsy of the supraclavicular node for confirmation and staging.
